in-lysmata-wurdemanni.title: Peppermint Shrimp
in-lysmata-wurdemanni.summary: A small shrimp best known for eating pest Aiptasia anemones.
rows: About 2 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 0.7 cm (0.3 in) CL (SeaLifeBase)
Carnivore scavenger. Picks leftovers and detritus; some individuals eat Aiptasia, others ignore it
notes: Not every shrimp will eat Aiptasia.

in-stenopus-hispidus.title: Banded Coral Shrimp
in-stenopus-hispidus.summary: A red-and-white banded "boxing shrimp" with large claws.
rows: Indo-Pacific and Western Atlantic: From the Red Sea and South Africa to Tuamotu Is., Hawaii and Easter Is
notes: Aggressive toward other banded coral shrimp and small shrimp, but usually peaceful with fish and corals.
Hides for a day or two when molting.

in-lysmata-debelius.title: Fire Shrimp
in-lysmata-debelius.summary: A deep red cleaner shrimp with white spots and long white antennae. Also called the Blood Red Fire Shrimp.
rows: Carnivore. Freeze-dried, live or frozen foods; also cleans parasites and dead tissue off fish
notes: Mostly active at night; wants caves and overhangs out of strong light.
warn: Like all invertebrates, it does not tolerate copper or high nitrate.

in-hymenocera-picta.title: Harlequin Shrimp
in-hymenocera-picta.sci: Hymenocera picta (some split Indian Ocean animals as H. elegans)
in-hymenocera-picta.summary: A striking spotted shrimp that eats only starfish. It flips a sea star over and feeds on its tube feet.
rows: About 1-1/2 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 5 cm (2 in) body length (SeaLifeBase)
Yes for corals, but it will eat any starfish in the tank
Starfish only. You must supply live starfish for it to eat
notes: Reaches about 2 in (5 cm); females are a little larger than males.

in-lysmata-amboinensis.title: Skunk Cleaner Shrimp
in-lysmata-amboinensis.summary: A cleaner shrimp that runs a cleaning station, picking parasites and dead tissue off fish.
rows: Carnivore. Meaty foods plus what it cleans from fish
notes: Many fish let it clean inside their mouths.
